title: First run: 38 questions with the answer written down first
changed: Ten sql questions where the answer turns on a definition: lift, new customer, regular, summer, net payout, item margin. The vendor's definitions are in the prompt. Each owner's own words are a Definitions document beside their policies, searched and cited like any other section.
Every gold query is its own file, headed by the question, so a reader can check it against the model's.

Fifteen policy questions, including two where the nearest section is the wrong one. Eight proposals that code has to check against the rules. Three questions that must be declined, one about the other restaurant, one that needs no search.

Twenty-four months of data with named menus, food costs, one price per item per channel, a promotion, loyalty rewards, seasonal items and regulars who stop coming, so these questions have answers in the data.
Retrieval threshold 0.50, a number picked from ten captured runs before this set existed.
conclusion: One wrong-but-safe query in ten. Two rules hidden by the retrieval threshold. One citation slip caught by code. The threshold moves to 0.40 next.

title: Second run: the retrieval threshold moves from 0.50 to 0.40
changed: One number changed, the similarity score a policy section needs before the model sees it, from 0.50 to 0.40. Nothing else: same questions, same gold, same model, same prompt.
conclusion: One case fewer, and a different set of failures. The rule hidden at 0.47 is now found. A question the policies do not cover now pulls in a near section, which the model dismisses correctly and my grader counts as a fail anyway. The citation slip happened a second time. Recall 86% to 93%, precision 46% to 29%. The threshold stays. The next change is the grader's rule for not-covered cases and the citation label, not the model.
